title: Self-hosted durable objects are pretty interesting!
text: Last week, Ryan Dahl, the creator of Deno, launched Svelte. And Svelte is quite interesting. It's a self-hosted distributed durable objects and workers implementation. What does that mean though? Durable objects are Cloudflare durable objects. It's a service by Cloudflare and it's a service that's all about giving you a worker with some extra stuff. Because a durable object in the end is just like a worker, an event handler function sitting somewhere in the cloud waiting for an event to happen. An event could be an HTTP request arriving at it, that would be quite common. It could also be a cron trigger. Cloudflare gives you different events you can use to trigger an event handler, a worker. You can think of it as AWS Lambda in case you know that. Now, a durable object is basically an enhanced version of that, which does not mean it's always better, but for certain use cases, it's better because a durable object has that event handler function or actually multiple functions if you need them as you'll see, but it also comes with persistent storage. Typically modern durable objects created on Cloudflare come with a SQLite storage attached and persistent really means persistent. It's not just for a few hours or definitely not for one request. Instead, it's there for weeks, months, years. It's really a function with some fixed storage attached to it. Great for building distributed systems since you can have different handlers for different events and every handler can memorize stuff and store data. To make this really useful though, every durable object also comes with a fixed address, which is kind of required so that a future request that is about the same thing can reach the same function and operate on the same data. Persistent data wouldn't be worth a lot if you had no way of controlling which request gets there. So that is a durable object. And unlike workers, it is also all about saving that storage or having that storage. Now, that's all good, but let's see some example maybe. And therefore the question is, why would you care? Why not just use Cloudflare Durable Objects? And the answer is control, predictability over pricing and cost, and potentially also cost savings. Control is clear, it's your server, you have full control over that. Predictability can be interesting because Durable Objects are really, really cheap. There is a very generous free limit, and if you got the workers paid plan, you got lots of invocations. It's really cheap. But depending on what you're running there, at some point the cheap part will not suffice anymore. And if you set something up in the wrong way, you could actually incur cost you did not anticipate.
